business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law heritage, U.S.-influenced corporate statutes, and Marshallese customary law; unitary national legal system without sub-fiscal jurisdictions)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States (1986; Amended 2003) — investment and economic relations provisions
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus — Pacific regional trade agreement in force for the Republic of the Marshall Islands
No standalone Bilateral Investment Treaty or comprehensive Double Taxation Agreement currently in force with non-Pacific states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2012 (as amended); Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BOCA), Title 27, Part 1 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code; Beneficial Ownership Regulations issued by the Registrar of Corporations; Registrar of Corporations AML/CFT Compliance Guidelines; National Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — beneficial ownership information is filed confidentially with the Registrar of Corporations and is not publicly searchable; registered agents must maintain an internal UBO register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and charter of each corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney and consent to act as first director(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if apostille not recognized)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each individual UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / public notary for address verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each beneficial owner, issued within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution maintaining the UBO's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank letter plus Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form and corporate structure breakdown identifying all individuals with 25% or greater ownership or control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille if signed outside the Marshall Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions, and RMI domestic designations under the AML/CFT Act. Politically Exposed Persons are subject to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Negative media and adverse regulatory checks are required for each UBO. All screening results must be preserved by the registered agent and made available to the Registrar of Corporations upon lawful request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations Online Corporate Registry and Name Reservation Portal (corporate.registrar.gov.mh)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in English/Latin script. Non-English terms must be transliterated into standard English romanization. The proposed name must be distinguishable from registered or reserved names and must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or permitted abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.' as applicable to a Marshall Islands Business Corporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended for one additional 30-day period by filing an extension request and paying the applicable fee before expiry. If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of rejection, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and compliance. The Registrar must decide within 10 business days. A further judicial appeal may be brought to the High Court of the Marshall Islands within 30 days after an adverse administrative decision. Government filing fees are non-refundable, and the applicant must submit a fresh name request if the appeal is ultimately denied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual/teleoperated business operations are permissible for a non-resident digital publishing entity, but a physical registered office in the Marshall Islands must be maintained through a licensed registered agent. No physical staff, assets, or local office lease is required for this industry at the pre-incorporation stage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated annualized probability below 5% for a standard-risk non-resident digital magazine publishing entity with no physical presence in the Marshall Islands and no adverse sanctions/PEP flags, based on risk-based supervision under the AML/CFT Act.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business Corporation Certificate of Incorporation (Government Filing Fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Business Corporations Act Fee Schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, Sections 32 (Incorporation), 35 (Registered Office), and 105 (Board of Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) filed pursuant to Section 32 of the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the corporation may issue shares without full payment; no escrow or bank deposit condition imposed on non-resident business corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Registrar of Corporations be, and hereby are, approved and adopted in their entirety; that the subscription for 10,000 common shares without par value, subscribed for by the founding shareholder, is accepted; that the registered office located at the registered agent's address in Majuro, Marshall Islands, is adopted; that the registered agent is retained and ratified; that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; that said officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute digital publishing contracts, and maintain the required corporate records; and all prior acts performed in furtherance of incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Records Pre-Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands (Online portal: www.rmicorporate.org)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request for the proposed corporate name. Ensure the name is distinguishable from existing registered entities and includes a title such as 'Corporation' or 'Incorporated'. Pay the reservation fee via the portal and obtain the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing for any parent entity (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, select an alternative name and refile. If no alternative name is available, file a written request for administrative review within 7 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Notary Public in the Marshall Islands or a Marshall Islands attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation, including: corporate name, purpose, share provisions, registered agent name and address in the Marshall Islands, and names/addresses of initial directors. The articles must be signed by the incorporator and notarized.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the articles, rectify the stated deficiency and resubmit. If the query concerns the registered agent, execute a new agent consent and upload within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation through the Marshall Islands online registry portal. Pay the filing fee of USD 250 using the electronic payment gateway. Track the submission using the referenced confirmation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for technical omissions, submit an amended filing within 10 business days. If the registrar requires additional information, respond to the query through the portal within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the Articles and receipt of fees, the Registrar issues the official Certificate of Incorporation. Download the certificate from the portal and retain it as part of the corporate records. The certificate serves as conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of receipt from online filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the prescribed SLA, send a written follow-up to the Registrar citing the filing reference. If clerical errors appear in the certificate, apply for a correction by filing a certificate of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and Initial Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial board meeting (in person or by unanimous consent) to adopt the corporate bylaws, register the issuance of shares to the founding shareholder, appoint officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), and approve the registered office address and agent. Prepare minutes of the meeting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer is unavailable, execute written ballots by unanimous consent. If the registered agent resigns, appoint a substitute agent and file the change with the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Republic of the Marshall Islands (for information purposes only)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing permit required for digital publishing activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Protection Authority, Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements produce no physical wastewater, atmospheric emissions, or solid waste discharges requiring assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated discharges; digital operations must comply with general municipal waste disposal rules and, if any office equipment is used, applicable WEEE (electronic waste) collection guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate or structural load inspection is mandated for mobile digital and remote operations. If physical offices are leased, obtain standard fire and safety clearances from island municipal authorities for offices with more than 10 occupants, in accordance with Marshall Islands civil defense standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands, Ministry of Finance – Revenue and Customs Division, Majuro; official portal: https://www.finance.gov.mh (paper-based filings; no separate online TIN issuance portal)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) is not required to obtain a national TIN or VAT ID for foreign-source digital publishing income. The sole statutory identifier is the corporate registration number issued by the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act 1990. If the BC should ever undertake RMI-source activities or hold a local business license, it must submit a paper application for a taxpayer identification number to the Revenue and Customs Division at the Ministry of Finance, attaching: (1) a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and current charter documents; (2) the registered agent's consent and address in the Marshall Islands; (3) a completed RMI Business License application; and (4) a declaration segregating anticipated RMI-source revenue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI tax law provides no check-the-box, disregarded-entity, or hybrid-mismatch elections. The exemption/classification of a non-resident Business Corporation is automatic if it has no income sourced in the Republic and no local branch or profit-seeking activity. The only administrative elections are the optional accelerated payment of annual corporate registration fees and the choice of cash or accrual basis for local business licensing purposes where an RMI-source activity is separately approved.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not Applicable – No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax (RMI indirect revenue is limited to customs duties and excise-type impositions on physical imports)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None – There is no taxable output-based indirect tax, no VAT threshold, and no registration obligation for digital magazine portal income. A physical importer of goods must be recorded with the Customs Division for each consignment regardless of value; all amounts are quantified in United States dollars.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. RMI mandates no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, tax authority API integration, or digital stamping. Digital media invoices and Stripe/AdSense payment records may be maintained in ordinary electronic format, subject to standard record-retention rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because RMI does not impose VAT/GST/SUT, there is no export zero-rating regime. Digital magazine subscriptions, advertising/sponsored media placements, and related payments processed through Stripe or AdSense are non-RMI source service income and are outside the scope of RMI indirect and income tax without requiring an export VAT claim. This status is conditional on: (i) no RMI office, branch, or dependent agent; (ii) no RMI-direct subscription revenue booked through an RMI establishment; and (iii) no physical media dispatched into RMI customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable – no RMI VAT export zero-rating refund claim can be filed.
Not applicable – no RMI customs export declaration is required solely for digital magazine export income.
Not applicable – no RMI inward remittance certificate is required for Stripe/AdSense payouts.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export-VAT clawback is possible because no VAT/GST zero-rating has ever been allowed. The Revenue and Customs Division may audit the entity's non-resident/exempt status. If the BC is found to have earned RMI-source income or to have maintained a local business presence without a license and without filing, the Division may assess the tax due for open statutory years, add interest, impose administrative penalties, and refer deliberate concealment to the Attorney-General for criminal prosecution. For false customs declarations in physical export contexts, RMI Customs may apply seizure and monetary penalties under the RMI Customs Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commission of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (prudential supervisor under the Banking Act 1991; the United States Dollar is domestic legal tender and there is no sovereign central bank of currency issue)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility prevails; the Marshall Islands maintains no exchange control statute, no foreign-exchange licensing regime, and no prior-approval mechanism for cross-border transfers. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation are unrestricted for non-resident business corporations, subject only to the annual franchise tax filing obligation and general anti-money-laundering reporting. The US Dollar being the domestic currency eliminates local convertibility risk for the digital publishing model, whose advertising and subscription revenue is predominantly USD-denominated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio exists under Marshall Islands law. Digital publishing and sponsored-media receipts may be retained indefinitely in USD or any freely convertible currency, with no prescribed remittance timeline, no mandatory conversion into local tender, and no registration threshold applicable to export-related earnings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam (Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Not applicable for commercial clearing or FX operations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. The Republic of the Marshall Islands has no domestic licensing framework for electronic money institutions or independent EMI charters; therefore, offshore digital EMIs may service an RMI business corporation only as unregulated money transmitters or under a foreign license, with settlement ultimately clearing through US correspondent banks. The Banking Act 1991 prohibits unlicensed deposit-taking within the RMI, and correspondent-bank de-risking of offshore digital media entities remains a practical threat. A licensed RMI bank or a US-licensed money transmitter is the preferred compliant rail for low-risk digital advertising payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of authorized signatories is generally expected at domestic licensed banks for in-person signature verification, although remote account opening may be approved where the compliance committee accepts video-KYC, notarized and apostilled corporate records, independent banker's references, and certified passport copies. Non-resident directors must supply original or certified corporate documentation, including Articles of Incorporation, By-Laws, Certificate of Good Standing, and Register of Directors and Shareholders, and the natural-person interview requirement is not waivable solely through legal counsel where anti-money-laundering rules mandate direct signatory identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident tax-exempt business corporation with no local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, current Certificate of Good Standing, annual report filing receipt, register of directors and shareholders, licensed registered agent confirmation letter, detailed business plan, and a beneficial ownership declaration identifying all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital advertising and sponsored-media revenue streams from AdSense and Stripe without audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month platform payout statements, advertiser and sponsorship contracts, customer and subscription invoices, traffic and content analytics evidence, interim management accounts or accountant-prepared financials, and sanctions and PEP screening results for material counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving counterparties in high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts evidencing the underlying media placement or subscription service, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations, bank reference letters, completed compliance questionnaire, and a clearing diagram demonstrating that no sanctioned or opaque intermediary participates in the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lump-sum inbound capital injection or related-party funding disproportionate to issued share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital contribution, subscription and share allotment agreements, identification of all funding shareholders, remitting-bank source-of-funds statement, tax-exempt status certificate, and a written memorandum establishing the commercial purpose and quantum of the injected amount.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 or MT202 bilateral wires initiated through licensed RMI banks, with final settlement across Fedwire or CHIPS in the United States clearing system given the US Dollar standard. No RMI regulatory approval or mandatory purpose code is required; remitters should state a descriptive narrative purpose such as 'capital contribution', 'share subscription', or 'intercompany loan', together with the corporate registry number. Verification consists of the remitting bank's source-of-funds statement, a board resolution, and beneficial ownership confirmation to satisfy both the Banking Commission and US correspondent-bank due diligence under the US Bank Secrecy Act expectations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and content-production disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for royalties, license fees, and service payments; commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP600 for high-value print or media supply contracts; US ACH and Fedwire for domestic US vendors; and internal book transfers between licensed RMI bank accounts. Correspondent clearing is USD-denominated without surrender or conversion constraints; outgoing instructions must include the beneficiary's full legal name, IBAN or account number, and an underlying invoice reference to prevent rejection or Office of Foreign Assets Control review delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated vanilla FX forwards executed with a licensed RMI or US bank
European-style FX options and covered currency swaps
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic or restricted emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps where the underlying commercial obligation is evidenced by contract

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Form AR) and Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through April 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$100; continued non-payment after April 30 subjects corporation to administrative strike-off and loss of good standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for non-resident Business Corporation; audit only triggered by shareholders agreement, lender covenant, or listing on a securities exchange
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No locally prescribed accounting framework; generally IFRS or US GAAP per management election and investor requirements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing for non-resident BC; registered agent must maintain current beneficial ownership records and any share transfer must be logged by the Board and recorded in the Register of Members

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$450 – US$1,200 depending on registered agent service level
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 – no statutory audit; voluntary audit typically US$5,000 – US$15,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident domestic corporations are wholly exempt from national income tax; no tax holidays or preferential deductions apply; annual fixed government fees (annual report/franchise fee) remain payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: None (no CIT return). Annual Corporate Statement / Annual Report and Government Fee filing via the RMI Registrar of Corporations online portal (RMI Online Corporate Registry; e-filing through licensed registered agents).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual report and government fee due on or before April 30 of each year following the calendar year of incorporation (or the anniversary date if required by the registered agent).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the Marshall Islands Business Corporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name on the Certificate of Incorporation; no tax classification election needed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and street address of the licensed RMI registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the registered agent's address in Majuro; non-resident entities cannot act as their own registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all directors and principal officers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee or resident directorship is permitted, but full beneficial-ownership data must be disclosed to the agent and Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of issued shares and class/par value
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required for annual fee computation; bearer shares are prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Brief description of activities conducted during the period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 'digital media publishing and advertising' (ISIC 5813); foreign-sourced revenue need not be reported to RMI tax authorities because no CIT is imposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual report: USD 100 late fee plus possible reinstatement fee; continued non-filing leads to administrative dissolution/strike-off, loss of good standing, and restrictions on bank account maintenance. No daily CIT surcharge applies.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No double taxation agreements (DTAs) enter into force for Marshall Islands corporations; therefore no treaty-relief procedure exists. If a foreign payer seeks evidence of residence, request a Certificate of Tax Residence / Good Standing from the RMI Registrar (through the registered agent); RMI does not certify tax residence for exempt non-resident companies because they are outside the RMI income tax net.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest; no treaty rates applicable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable (no RMI transfer-pricing or Local/Master File rules); for foreign parent filings, maintain TP documentation at the OECD standard if intra-group transactions exceed USD 10 million (local currency is USD).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019/2021 requires entities carrying on 'relevant activities' (e.g., distribution and service centers, headquarters, IP business, financing/leasing) to maintain economic presence in RMI. A digital magazine publishing and sponsored-media portal is not typically a listed relevant activity unless it also holds IP or acts as a distribution/service center; nevertheless, the entity must not present itself as an RMI-resident taxpayer and must preserve demonstrable offshore management to retain the non-resident exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Managing the corporation's digital operations, executing contracts, or holding board decisions inside the Marshall Islands while declaring non-resident status, or using the RMI entity to disguise profits of a foreign beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification as an RMI-resident taxpayer; imposition of national income tax (if income is RMI-source) plus penalties up to 100% of the tax due and cancellation of exempt status. Administrative fines under the Business Corporations Act for false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the corporation's tax and penalties if they signed false certificates; fraudulent incorporation or evasive filing may result in director disqualification, injunctions, and criminal imprisonment under the RMI Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a purely passive digital-ad-revenue vehicle with no operational substance, no physical presence, no real staff, and no records, while claiming RMI non-resident tax benefits; failure to file annual report or to disclose beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations, a finding of non-compliance can result in monetary penalties up to USD 10,000 for first offence, USD 20,000 for continuing default, and possible exchange of information with foreign tax authorities; registration may be struck off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers of a struck-off shell corporation may face restoration costs, personal fines for continued trading, and a direction to wind up; ultimate beneficial owners are exposed under money-transparency laws.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing the controlling shareholder(s) or using nominee directors to move AdSense/Stripe payouts through the RMI entity without filing the required beneficial-ownership particulars to the registered agent; receiving funds without maintaining AML/KYC policies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Regulations, unlicensed non-compliance attracts fines of up to USD 100,000 per violation for entities, with remedial orders; the corporate registration can be suspended. The RMI is not a FATF blacklisted jurisdiction, but certain non-cooperative flags trigger restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to criminal liability (imprisonment up to 5 years) for complicity in money laundering, travel bans issued by RMI courts, and confiscation of personal assets in civil forfeiture proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing materially false information in the annual corporate statement (e.g., understating issued shares, concealing changes in directors, or affirming non-resident status when management is conducted from the Marshall Islands).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalty of up to USD 25,000 under the Business Corporations Act; possible involuntary dissolution with the loss of the RMI legal personality and inability to enforce contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers face personal civil liability for damages to creditors and shareholders, and criminal fines; courts may pierce the corporate veil to hold directors jointly and severally liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the digital magazine portal as an unlicensed money-transfer business by processing third-party sponsored-media payments or using Stripe/AdSense balances as a quasi-payment system without authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Banking and Trust Act, operating a money transmission business without a license is a criminal offence with fines and imprisonment for up to 7 years; all transaction records may be seized and the corporate bank accounts frozen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or fail to prevent unlicensed payment activity can be held personally criminally liable and subject to imprisonment; the corporate veil will be pierced for equitable restitution to defrauded advertisers.
